text: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise takes the caller identity from the session, the capability area CASE_RECORD, the right R, the case reference, the plan reference, the field IDs the panel will show and the case attributes the scope test needs (owner, queue and team), and answers with the decision code (AC-READ or AC-DENY), the matrix version, the scope result and the access-entry reference; GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions answers the caller's roles, the CASE_RECORD letters in force, the scope and the matrix version, for the caller's own record only.
why: Architecture v5 names both operations and the TSD appendix does not, so the request and answer shapes have to be fixed as a default before the build; leaving them empty would stop the story, and whether the plan reference travels in the request decides whether the caller passes it or resolves it.

text: The rwb-access database login keeps the service naming convention (schema rwb_access with one login) and is named 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' in the story until the platform DB story fixes the name; this slice adds no REST path of its own and rewrites no TSD entry.
why: The legacy story names no login and the platform DB story has not fixed the per-service login names, and the story must not invent a credential name.

text: The plan-status policy pack slice is read as the matrix version in force: CASE_RECORD right R for RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT and RW-AUDIT, no CASE_RECORD row for RW-REFADM, default scope OWN for RW-CASEOWN, OWN for RW-RESTRUCT and ALL for RW-AUDIT, at matrix version PM-2026.12, with no masking row because the panel carries no personal field; a second version of the matrix on one business date is resolved to the version whose latest valid_from is on or before the business date.
why: The TSD RBAC matrix has no Case record column while the legacy authority table and the plan-status path need the letter, so the letters and scopes are read from the pack as data rather than from a table, and two versions on one date need one rule.

text: The composite route of SCR-03 Case record calls rwb-case for the case and the stored plan status, rwb-integration for the live plan status and rwb-access for the resolved view and the decision, one hop each, in parallel, and merges the answers into the panel model; the panel shows the plan reference, the status and the status date only, so no masking row applies and nothing is masked, and the route path, its field list and its merge order are the edge contract's and are not fixed here.
why: The legacy screen was served by the monolith, the split gives the panel three providers, and no source fixes the route path, the panel field list or the field-level masking of the composite answer, so a readable default is recorded instead of invented in code.
